Gangaram Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12
January, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:1319
 1 Mcrc
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta

On The 12th Of January, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 58094 of 2025
 Gangaram Ahirwar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Abhinav Bhargav - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Mohit Shivhare - Pp for the State.
 Order

The applicant has filed this first bail application under Section 482 of the BNSS for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant for the offence registered at Crime No.132/2025 at Police Station- Bamorkalan, District Shivpuri for offence punishable under Sections 296(A), 115(2), 326(G), 351(2),
3(5) of BNS.
2 .

The prosecution story, in brief, is that on 31.10.2025 an FIR was lodged at Police Station Bamorkala by the complainant stating that on the same day, at approximately 2:00 PM, when she was cooking in her hut near house of Patel Sahib in Bamorkala, then Gangaram Ahirwar, his son namely Rahul Ahirwar, Dinesh Ahirwar, and Chhotu Ahirwar came there and asked her to leave,
claiming that they had leased the land from Ramesh Chandra Jain.
Complainant stated that she had NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:1319 2 MCRC-58094-2025 been living and cultivating the land for about 15 years and they could not force her to leave.
Thereupon, all the persons started verbally abusing her using vulgar language.
When she objected, then Rahul Ahirwar slapped her and Gangaram Ahirwar grabbed her hand and threw her to the ground.

Thereafter,
Dinesh Ahirwar and Chhotu Ahirwar assaulted her with kicks and fists due to which she sustained many injuries in her body parts.
Thereafter, all the accused persons set her hut on fire.

Upon her raising an alarm, her husband Amol Lodhi, son of complainant Golu Lodhi and Rajiv Jain from Jainpath Hotel who were working in the nearby field came to her rescue and intervened in the matter.
By that time, other persons had also gathered at the spot and helped in extinguishing the fire.

As a result of the fire, her household articles, bedding, food items and cash amounting to Rs.2,000/- kept in the hut were destroyed which causing an estimated loss of approximately Rs.20,000/- to Rs.25,000/-.

While leaving the spot, all the accused alongwith present applicant Gangaram Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157249326/
1 threatened her stating that although she had been saved on this occasion, they would kill her if she continued to stay there.

sentences.text: On the basis of the incident, the offence has been registered under Section 296(a), 115(2), 326(g), 351(2), and 3(5) of the BNS and investigation has been initiated.
3 . It is the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that false case has been registered against the applicant.
He has not committed any such incident and he does not have any direct or indirect NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:1319 3 MCRC-58094-2025 connection with the said crime.
The applicant is a poor farmer belonging to the Scheduled Caste community and earns his livelihood by sharecropping on agricultural land owned and possessed by Ramesh Chandra Jain.

This FIR has been registered solely to put pressure on the applicant because the applicant and his family members had already lodged an FIR against the complainant party and his family members in which the complainant and his family members assaulted the applicant and his family members by threatening them with dire consequences and used caste-based derogatory remarks.
It is further submitted that the whole story is created by the complainant in collusion with the police.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has already been filed.
Applicant does not bear any criminal record.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Applicant would abide by the terms and conditions as imposed by this Court.
Under these grounds, he prayed for bail.
4. Learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and submitted that the allegations against the applicant are grave, serious and supported by specific and direct accusations.

The FIR clearly discloses that the applicant along with other co-accused persons committed criminal trespass, voluntarily caused hurt, used criminal force, issued criminal intimidation and committed arson, resulting in physical injuries to the complainant and substantial loss of property.

Therefore, anticipatory bail application filed by the applicant may be NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:1319 4 MCRC-58094-2025 rejected.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6 . Upon a complete consideration of the incident, the ingredients of Section 435 of the IPC are not attracted against the applicant.
The allegations, even if taken at their face value, do not disclose any act or intention on the part of the applicant so as to constitute the offence under the said provision.
7 . In the present case, the role of the applicant is specific and active.

The applicant not only participated in abusing and assaulting the complainant but also, along with co-accused persons, set the complainant's hut on fire, thereby attracting Section 326(g) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,
which relates to serious offences involving fire and destruction of property.
Such offences are heinous in nature and have a serious impact on public order and the safety of the victim.
The injuries sustained by the complainant have been medically examined and prima facie evidence supports the prosecution case.

The investigation is at a crucial stage and custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary to ascertain the complete chain of events, to recover evidence and identify the involvement of other persons.
Benefit of grant of anticipatory bail at this stage would seriously hamper a fair and effective investigation.

sentences.text: Furthermore, the complainant has specifically stated that the applicant threatened to kill her if she continued to reside on the disputed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:1319 5 MCRC-58094-2025 land.
There is a strong likelihood that if anticipatory bail is granted, the applicant may influence witnesses, threaten the complainant, or tamper with evidence.

9 . In view of the seriousness of the offences, the specific role attributed to the applicant, the threat perception to the complainant and the ongoing investigation, the applicant is not entitled to the discretionary relief of anticipatory bail.
Hence, the anticipatory bail application is hereby dismissed.
